text:
maria: FYI nightly perf job failed on kernel-selection kv-cache microbench. CI run shows a missing nsys artifact and a spike in tail latency. link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/2147654321

sam: link? I saw spiking latencies in the perf dashboard earlier this morning.

dinesh: is this the eager selector path or the deferred path? which KV hot path?

maria: looks like the selector fell back to a generic kernel repeatedly; KV cache lookups were fine but the chosen kernel kept returning transient errors. nsys capture was omitted because file size hit quota. full logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/2147654321/console

sam: can you re-run with nsys in continuous capture but limited to the process PID and a short window? e.g.

```bash
nsys profile --output=ci_trace --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite \\
  --sleep=0 --duration=120 --pid=12345
```

elena: also consider `--sample-mode=clock` to keep file sizes down. continuous captures balloon if there are lots of small kernels. set `--trace-fork-exec=no` in CI to cut unrelated noise.

ryan: we hit a similar symptom when the kernel selector loop spun after a kernel load returned -EAGAIN. that usually means a kernel binary mismatch or driver scheduling hiccup. we should capture kernel binary metadata with the trace artifact so the diff dashboard can correlate.

dinesh: +1. include `uname -a`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and a sha256sum of the kernel .so files in artifact metadata. that helps rule out host/kernel differences.

maria: adding a small snippet to the CI job to collect env + kernel metadata and push to S3:

```bash
# collect env + kernel metadata
echo "HOST_INFO: $(uname -a)" > meta.txt
nvidia-smi -q >> meta.txt
sha256sum /opt/models/*/kernels/*.so >> meta.txt || true
# compress trace and upload
gzip -c ci_trace.qdrep > ci_trace.qdrep.gz
aws s3 cp ci_trace.qdrep.gz s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/2147654321/ci_trace.qdrep.gz
aws s3 cp meta.txt s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/2147654321/meta.txt
```

sam: can we also run `nsys stats` to emit a small JSON summary for the diff dashboard? raw qdrep diffs are too big to diff regularly.

elena: yes, run `nsys stats --output=summary --format=json ci_trace.qdrep` and upload the summary. that JSON is what the nightly diff pipeline should ingest.

ci-bot: @maria scheduled rerun with updated capture flags (job #5421). artifacts will be saved to s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/2147654321/.

maria: thanks. I'll include kernel-version and sm_arch in the summary so diffs can group by hardware.

ryan: also bump the CI runner memory cap for the nightly capture to avoid OOM during compression. `--memory 12G` on the runner did the trick last time.

dinesh: did the rerun finish? any obvious hotspot from the trace?

ci-bot: job #5421 completed, summary: top kernel 'gemm_smem_128x128' median grew from 3.2ms -> 8.1ms, kernel binary hash mismatch detected (sha256: old=aa3f... new=8c7d...). raw: s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/2147654321/ci_trace.qdrep.gz, summary: s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/2147654321/summary.json

maria: good catch. opening a small PR to pin kernel builds in the CI image and to add an artifact-hash check that will fail the job when kernel binaries drift. assigning to @dinesh for the selector rollback path.

sam: if we pin kernels, add a safe rollback path so the runtime selector can fallback to the previous kernel binary when a new one yields worse latency.

elena: added a runbook note with the updated capture flags, metadata checklist, and artifact retention policy (keep 30 days).

maria: thx all :thumbsup:
